title: A Rubisco combining high CO2 specificity with high turnover

concept.text: Millennium Problems for Biology 4, Improve Rubisco. Target: a Rubisco with CO2/O2 specificity at least as high as Galdieria partita Rubisco and turnover (kcat) at least as high as maize Rubisco, measured in paired assays against those controls. Sources given: https://millenniumproblems.bio/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to BOT on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the twelve Millennium Problems for Biology (Sam Rodriques and Michaela Hinks, FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, 2026), each with a stated concrete target; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Rubisco with Galdieria partita specificity and maize turnover
page.definition: A Rubisco enzyme that carboxylates ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate with CO₂/O₂ specificity at least that of Galdieria partita and turnover at least that of maize. Specificity is the ratio of catalytic efficiencies for CO₂ and O₂; turnover is the maximum number of carboxylations per active site per second.

goal.need: Rubisco fixes around 100 Gt of carbon annually. Published kinetics illustrate the separation between the desired properties: Galdieria partita Rubisco has higher CO₂/O₂ specificity, whereas maize Rubisco has faster carboxylation turnover. Combining these properties addresses both carbon fixation rate and the competing oxygenation reaction.

completion.title: One Rubisco matches G. partita specificity and maize turnover in paired enzyme assays.
completion.criterion: One candidate enzyme must catalyse ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylation with CO₂/O₂ specificity at least that of Galdieria partita Rubisco and carboxylation turnover at least that of maize Rubisco. Measure specificity in paired enzyme assays using G. partita Rubisco as the control, and turnover in paired enzyme assays using maize Rubisco as the control. The candidate may be discovered in nature, engineered, evolved or designed de novo.
completion.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, Millennium Problems for Biology, Problem 04; the initial list was published on 19 September 2026.
completion.basis: This is the organisers’ explicit acceptance criterion for Problem 04. It requires one catalyst to combine both comparator properties. The final two milestones below are its component tests and can be reached independently. Historical kinetic values provide context; the paired controls determine the acceptance thresholds.

milestones.title: An engineered Rubisco has a higher carboxylation turnover than its parental enzyme.
milestones.criterion: Purified engineered and parental Rubisco are compared for substrate-saturated carboxylation turnover per active site, and the engineered enzyme has the higher value. Greene and colleagues demonstrated this laboratory result with Synechococcus PCC6301 M259T: 12.8 ± 0.2 s⁻¹ versus 11.4 ± 0.1 s⁻¹ for wild type at 25 °C, reported as means ± SD from three measurements per enzyme.
milestones.set_by: Rubisco engineering community; parental-enzyme kinetic comparisons applied by Greene, Whitney and Matsumura (2007), Table 2, and Gionfriddo and colleagues (2025).
milestones.threshold_quote: a 12% increase in carboxylation turnover rate

milestones.title: A Rubisco matches or exceeds Galdieria partita’s CO₂/O₂ specificity.
milestones.criterion: A candidate Rubisco has a CO₂/O₂ specificity factor at least as high as Galdieria partita Rubisco, measured in paired enzyme assays with G. partita Rubisco as the control. This is the specificity component of Problem 04. The table records the historical reference-enzyme result; that literature value alone does not establish a candidate’s paired-control result.
milestones.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, Millennium Problems for Biology, Problem 04; the specificity component of its published acceptance criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: as high as that of Galdieria Partita Rubisco

milestones.title: A Rubisco matches or exceeds maize’s carboxylation turnover.
milestones.criterion: A candidate Rubisco has carboxylation turnover at least as high as maize Rubisco, measured in paired enzyme assays with maize Rubisco as the control. This is the turnover component of Problem 04. The two comparator milestones can be demonstrated with different enzymes; completion requires both properties in one enzyme.
milestones.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, Millennium Problems for Biology, Problem 04; the turnover component of its published acceptance criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: as high as that of maize Rubisco.

not_found: No published result passing both paired-control comparisons in one Rubisco was located.
No Problem 04 assay specification fixing temperature, pH, replicate numbers or statistical acceptance was located.
The original 1997 Galdieria partita kinetic paper could not be opened; the comparator table uses the published compilation by Oh and colleagues.

results.finding: Purified Synechococcus PCC6301 M259T Rubisco showed a 12% increase in carboxylation turnover versus wild type (n=3 measurements per enzyme).
results.detail: At 25 °C, turnover was 12.8 ± 0.2 s⁻¹ for M259T and 11.4 ± 0.1 s⁻¹ for wild type (means ± SD). Maximal carboxylation activity was divided by the concentration of active sites.

results.finding: Purified T. kodakarensis Rubisco SP5-V330T: carboxylation turnover 0.53 s⁻¹ per site; sample size not reported.
results.detail: The parental wild-type enzyme had a turnover of 0.31 s⁻¹ per site. Measurements were made in vitro at ambient temperature.

results.finding: Purified tobacco Rubisco T391I had 29% higher carboxylation turnover than its parent; sample size not stated.
results.detail: At 25°C, turnover was 4.5 ± 0.4 s⁻¹ for T391I versus 3.5 ± 0.5 s⁻¹ for the parental enzyme, reported as means ± SD. Measurements were normalized to active-site counts.
results.quote: Most prominently, the T391I substitution improved carboxylation rate by 29% and aerobic carboxylation efficiency by 43%.

results.finding: Pennisetum purpureum Rubisco, n=3 independent measurements, had a mean carboxylation turnover of 3.92 s⁻¹.
results.detail: Maize Rubisco averaged 3.05 s⁻¹ under the same assay method, but the paper does not report paired assays using maize as the control; its statistical comparisons used rice.
